title: The mind is made of food
hook: why many Hindu homes offer food to God first: a father tells his son to stop eating, then asks him to recite the Vedas
carry: the mind is made of food
tomorrow: sleep: the bird returns to the tree

segments.voice: Yesterday: trivrit, red for heat, white for water, black for food. Your line was name and form, one Being beneath. Today ends week two of year two.

In many Hindu homes, a fresh meal doesn't start at the table. A little of it goes to the family shrine first, offered to God, and comes back as prasad, a gift, before anyone eats. Why so much care over food? Part of the answer is in today's story. Uddalaka tells his son the mind is made of food, and then he proves it, with his own son as the test.
screen: `A LITTLE GOES TO GOD FIRST.` → `IT COMES BACK AS PRASAD.` → `WHY SO MUCH CARE OVER FOOD?`

segments.voice: Here's what happens to the three stuffs once they're inside you, Uddalaka says. Food, when eaten, divides into three. The coarsest part leaves the body. The middle part becomes flesh. The finest part becomes mind. Water divides the same way: the coarsest leaves, the middle becomes blood, the finest becomes breath. Heat, eaten in rich things like oil and ghee, as teachers explain it, divides too: its coarsest part becomes bone, the middle marrow, the finest speech. So mind is made of food, breath of water, speech of heat. Shvetaketu says, please, tell me more. So his father gives him an experiment. Don't eat for fifteen days. Drink water as you like, since breath is made of water. Shvetaketu fasts, comes back, and his father says: recite the Vedas. He can't. Nothing comes, sir. His father gives a picture: when a great fire has burned down to one ember the size of a firefly, it can't burn much. But add straw, and it blazes again. Go eat. Shvetaketu eats, comes back, and now he can answer every question. The mind is made of food, my dear. Seven days this week, in one breath: the guru who points inward. Life as an offering. The one thing worth knowing. Many names, one clay. One Being becoming many. Name and form. And today, food becoming mind. The Chandogya won't separate the sacred from the stomach. Many teachers read this as one root of the care Hindu homes give to food: if food becomes mind, then what you eat, and how it's offered, is part of your practice.
screen: `FOOD, WATER, HEAT: EACH IN THREE.` · `FIFTEEN DAYS WITHOUT FOOD.` · `THE EMBER AND THE STRAW.` · `THE SACRED AND THE STOMACH.` · then, large: `THE MIND IS MADE OF FOOD.`

segments.voice: Before your next meal, or with a glass of water right now, pause. Many Hindu families offer the food to God first, and many say a short prayer from the Bhagavad Gita before eating: brahmarpanam: the act of offering is Brahman, and what is offered is Brahman. If you don't pray, let the pause be gratitude. Then eat or drink slowly, knowing some of it will become the mind that's noticing.
Food. In Uddalaka's lesson, the finest part of food becomes mind, as the finest part of water becomes breath, and of heat, speech.
Your line: the mind is made of food. Annamayam hi somya manah. Week two of year two, done.

screen: `DAY 343 COUNTS.` → `WEEK TWO OF YEAR TWO, DONE.` → `TOMORROW: SLEEP.`

howItsDone: In Hindu homes food is often offered to God before it is eaten, and traditions of mindful eating and dietary practice connect what one eats with the clarity of the mind.
